punctuated: 其所有而不蓄矣；情發於人，人不愛其情，盡所有而發之矣。故膏露降于天也，其澤如膏之濃，而異乎常露；醴泉出乎地也，其味如醴之甘，而異乎常泉。山出乎器車，為希世之物；河出乎馬圖，為文明之瑞。鳳皇、麒麟，世不常有也，今皆在於郊內之棷；靈龜、神龍，人不常見也，今皆在於宮中之沼。其餘鳥之卵、獸之胎，皆可俯而闚，而無獝狘之患。天地人物同一大順如此，豈無故而然哉？由先王能脩此禮以為教，而達之天下無不宜；反身而誠，而達之天下無不順也。順理淵微，初無形象，今天地人物無不協應，昭然可見，非大順之實乎？吁！先王大順之實，著于天地人物之間，其功至此已極矣。抑考上文「四體既正」以下，極言大順之事也；「故事大積焉而不苑」以下，極言大順之理也；「故禮之大同」以下，又言順道之應也。至此又極言其大順之實，《中庸》所謂「致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉」，即此意矣。有天下者，其可忽諸！
translation_en: …all that it possesses without holding anything in reserve; and feelings spring from humanity, so humanity does not begrudge its feelings, expressing all that it possesses to the fullest. Therefore, sweet dew descends from Heaven, its moisture as rich as fat and different from ordinary dew; sweet springs gush forth from the Earth, their taste as sweet as new wine and different from ordinary springs. The mountains bring forth ceremonial carriages, which are treasures rarely seen in the world; the Yellow River brings forth the horse-chart, which is an auspicious omen of civilization. Phoenixes and unicorns (qilin) are not regularly found in the world, yet now they are all in the marshes within the suburbs; spirit tortoises and divine dragons are not regularly seen by people, yet now they are all in the ponds within the palace. As for the rest—the eggs of birds and the unborn young of beasts—all can be bent over and peered at without the alarm of their fleeing in terror. That Heaven, Earth, humanity, and all things share in one Great Harmony (dashun) like this—how could it be so without a cause? It is because the Former Kings were able to cultivate ritual propriety to serve as instruction, extending it throughout the realm so that nothing was inappropriate; and by examining themselves to be sincere in body, they extended it throughout the realm so that nothing failed to be in harmony. The principle of harmony is profound and subtle, originally without visible form; yet now Heaven, Earth, humanity, and all things respond in concert without exception, clearly manifest for all to see—is this not the reality of Great Harmony? Alas! The reality of the Former Kings' Great Harmony was manifested between Heaven, Earth, humanity, and all things; their achievement reached its ultimate pinnacle in this. Moreover, if we examine the preceding text, from "When the four limbs are properly aligned" onward, it speaks exhaustively of the affairs of Great Harmony; from "Therefore, affairs may accumulate greatly without becoming tangled" onward, it speaks exhaustively of the principle of Great Harmony; and from "Therefore, the Great Unity of ritual propriety" onward, it speaks further of the responses to the Way of harmony. Coming to this passage, it speaks exhaustively once more of the reality of Great Harmony. What the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) calls "achieving equilibrium and harmony, so that Heaven and Earth are in their proper places and the myriad things are nourished" expresses this very meaning. How could one who possesses the realm neglect this!

Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Luo 羅 comments: On this topic, scholars frequently repeat hackneyed phrases, which I had grown weary of reading for days on end. Late in the process I obtained this paper, which excels in both diction and principle. Moreover, the conclusion is especially marvelous; reading it suddenly opens one's mind and eyes. Even a jade disk worth a string of cities or a pearl that illuminates a dozen carriages could hardly be treasured more! Examiner Expositor-in-waiting Xu 徐 comments: It explains the symbolizing of achievement most incisively.

From the grand completion of the Martial Dance and the return to the initial position, it symbolizes the Sage returning to his state and occupying the supreme position. Now, music is that which symbolizes achievement. When the Sage achieved his martial功 (merit) and returned to his state to occupy the supreme position, does not the return to the starting line in the sixth movement of the musical dance symbolize this? Formerly, when Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) discussed music with Bin Mou Jia 賓牟賈 and instructed him, it was as if to say: In the music of King Wu 武王, the positions of the dance are six, and the movements of the music are also six, and what the movements complete has that which it symbolizes. title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第一位又非象武王大定之後而反于西土天
下皆崇之為皇王乎夫武王之歸鎬京非徒三
千師旅同心以尊之也而四海仰其永清之功
莫不尊之為天子以撫綏乎方夏矣武王之反
西土非徒八百諸侯同會以崇之也而四方服
其寵綏之德莫不崇之為皇王以奄甸乎萬姓
矣樂舞之六成而復初位不象乎此而奚象哉
孔子以是告賓牟賈其發明武樂之義至此可
謂盡矣抑不特此上文既曰總干而山立武王
===
之事也下文又曰夾振之而駟伐盛威於中國
也分夾而進事蚤濟也久立於綴以待諸侯之
至也盖武王以征誅而得天下故其樂如此若
舜之樂則奏諸朝廷而庶尹允諧百獸率舞奏
諸廟堂而祖考來格鳳凰來儀矣孔子謂韶盡
美矣又盡善也武盡美矣未盡善也良有以夫
第貳塲
論
國家一統之盛

punctuated:
第一位，又非象武王大定之後而反于西土，天下皆崇之為皇王乎？夫武王之歸鎬京，非徒三千師旅同心以尊之也，而四海仰其永清之功，莫不尊之為天子以撫綏乎方夏矣；武王之反西土，非徒八百諸侯同會以崇之也，而四方服其寵綏之德，莫不崇之為皇王以奄甸乎萬姓矣。樂舞之六成而復初位，不象乎此而奚象哉？孔子以是告賓牟賈，其發明《武》樂之義，至此可謂盡矣。抑不特此，上文既曰「總干而山立，武王之事也」，下文又曰「夾振之而駟伐，盛威於中國也；分夾而進，事蚤濟也；久立於綴，以待諸侯之至也」。盖武王以征誅而得天下，故其樂如此。若舜之樂，則奏諸朝廷而庶尹允諧、百獸率舞，奏諸廟堂而祖考來格、鳳凰來儀矣。孔子謂「《韶》盡美矣，又盡善也；《武》盡美矣，未盡善也」，良有以夫！

第貳塲

論

國家一統之盛
translation_en:
… the first position—does this not also symbolize how, after the great pacification, King Wu returned to the western lands, and all under Heaven revered him as August Sovereign? Now, when King Wu returned to his capital at Haojing, it was not merely his three thousand troops who were of one mind in honoring him; rather, all within the four seas looked up to his achievement of bringing lasting peace, and none failed to honor him as the Son of Heaven to pacify and comfort the central Chinese states. And when King Wu returned to the western lands, it was not merely the eight hundred feudal lords who assembled together to revere him; rather, the four quarters submitted to his favor and comforting virtue, and none failed to revere him as August Sovereign to rule over and govern the myriad people. When the musical dance reaches its sixth movement and returns to the initial position, if it does not symbolize this, what else could it symbolize? When Confucius told this to Bin Mou Jia, his elucidation of the meaning of the *Wu* music could be said to have reached its fullest extent here. Yet it is not only this. Above, the text already says, "Holding the shields and standing like a mountain is the deed of King Wu"; below, it further says, "Striking the bells in accompaniment and thrusting four times displays great majesty in the Central Kingdom; dividing into two ranks and advancing represents the early completion of the enterprise; standing long at the starting line is waiting for the arrival of the feudal lords." For King Wu obtained the Empire through punitive expeditions and conquest, and therefore his music was like this. As for the music of Shun, when performed in the court, all the officials were in true harmony and the hundred beasts led one another in dance; when performed in the ancestral temple, the spirits of the ancestors came and were present, and the phoenixes came with stately bearing. When Confucius said that the *Shao* was "perfectly beautiful and also perfectly good," whereas the *Wu* was "perfectly beautiful, but not yet perfectly good," he truly had good reason indeed!

Second Session

Discourse

"The Flourishing of the State's Great Unification"

text:
俟吾
同考試官訓導鄭批發揮一統之盛有考據有議論
如長江大河一瀉千里真有學士也
同考試官訓導鄭批此卷初塲七篇俱粹二塲獨
壓衆作表而出之其容疑議
考試官侍講徐批議論美文辭蒼古超出衆作
考試官洗馬楊批文章先體製而後工拙塲中
論作表體策體者至衆此篇庶得論體而敬
君之誠尤至非獨其辭之偉也可以式矣
===
天下之勢或渙而萬或萃而一自開闢以
来能萃天下於渙合萬而一之者僅可僂
數然皆未有若我
大明一統之盛者也愚嘗讀九丘誦禹貢覽
周職方考兩漢以下之圖志質之經訂之
史信乎一統之莫盛於今也自周之衰判
而十二併而為七三國鼎分南北瓜裂秦
晋及隋雖幸一之而電起漚滅曽何足齒

Hao Wu 俟吾.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zheng: In elaborating upon the flourishing of the Grand Unity, this essay possesses both textual evidence and critical discourse. Like the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers pouring forth a thousand *li*, the author is truly a scholar of learning.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zheng: The seven essays of the first session in this candidate's examination paper are all pure and refined, while the second session alone outshines all other compositions. When we single it out for distinction, how could there be room for any doubt or dispute?

Comment by Examiner and Expositor-in-waiting Xu: The argumentation is admirable and the diction is vigorous and antique, surpassing all other compositions.

Comment by Examiner and Librarian Yang: In literary composition, proper structural form comes first and technical skill second. In the examination hall, those who wrote the discourse in the style of a memorial or a policy essay were exceedingly numerous. This piece comes close to grasping the proper form of a discourse, and its sincerity in revering the sovereign is especially utmost. It is not merely the grandeur of its diction; it may serve as a model!

The momentum of the realm either scatters into myriad parts or gathers into a single unity. Since the creation of the world, those who have been able to gather the realm out of dispersion and unite the myriad parts into one can barely be counted on the fingers, yet none has ever matched the flourishing of the Grand Unity of our Great Ming. I have read the Nine Regions (*Jiuqiu*), recited the Tribute of Yu (*Yugong*), perused the職方 (*Zhifang*, Directions of the Realm) of the Zhou, and examined the maps and treatises from the Two Han dynasties onward. Verifying them against the Classics and collating them with the Histories, truly no unification has ever been more flourishing than that of the present day! Since the decline of the Zhou, the realm split into twelve states and consolidated into seven; the Three Kingdoms stood divided like the legs of a tripod, and North and South were carved up like a melon. Although the Qin, Jin, and Sui were fortunate enough to unify it, they flashed like lightning and vanished like bubbles on water—how could they even be worth mentioning? As for the True Man at Bashang [Liu Bang], who pressed the Qin and slew Xiang Yu, he unified the realm to become the Han…

text:
也龍姿日表濟世安民又一統而為唐也
聖人應祝而生受周之禪又一統而為宋
也然嫚書之遺椎髻之侵改為周國離為
列鎮北藩無燕雲中世有金元若此而謂
之一統之盛可乎元以腥羶汙我華夏
天寔厭之肆命我
太祖高皇帝以大聖之德乘
飛龍之運左伊而右仲前旦而後望
天戈一揮四方響應奮自歷陽飛渡天塹定
===
鼎于金陵於是殲強漢殪偽吳帖荆楚服
閩廣輯山之東西與河之南北既拔元都
遂擣關陝以掃巴蜀以拾滇南萬方來同
四夷來王合天下之疆土而郡縣之合天
下之塞徼而城溝之合天下之農而畛畝
之合天下之士而庠序之合天下之商工
而市肆之合天下之夷狄而冠裳之賞善
有爵罰惡有刑而天下不敢玩也足國有
賦衛民有兵而天下不敢違也會同有禮

punctuated: 也。龍姿日表，濟世安民，又一統而為唐也。聖人應祝而生，受周之禪，又一統而為宋也。然嫚書之遺，椎髻之侵；改為周國，離為列鎮；北藩無燕、雲，中世有金、元。若此而謂之一統之盛，可乎？元以腥羶汙我華夏，天寔厭之，肆命我太祖高皇帝，以大聖之德，乘飛龍之運，左伊而右仲，前旦而後望。天戈一揮，四方響應。奮自歷陽，飛渡天塹，定鼎于金陵。於是殲強漢，殪偽吳，帖荆、楚，服閩、廣，輯山之東西與河之南北。既拔元都，遂擣關、陝，以掃巴、蜀，以拾滇南。萬方來同，四夷來王。合天下之疆土而郡縣之，合天下之塞徼而城溝之，合天下之農而畛畝之，合天下之士而庠序之，合天下之商工而市肆之，合天下之夷狄而冠裳之。賞善有爵，罰惡有刑，而天下不敢玩也；足國有賦，衛民有兵，而天下不敢違也；會同有禮，
translation_en:
…. With dragon-like bearing and a sun-like countenance, bringing relief to the world and peace to the people, the realm was once again unified as the Tang. When a sage was born in answer to prayers and received the abdication of the Later Zhou, the realm was once again unified as the Song. Yet under the Han there was the insult of the insolent letter sent by the Xiongnu and the incursions of mallet-haired barbarians; under the Tang the dynasty was usurped and renamed Zhou, and the realm was fractured into autonomous military garrisons; under the Song the northern frontier lacked the Prefectures of Yan and Yun, and in its middle period it was confronted by the Jin and the Yuan. When things were like this, how could one call it the flourishing of grand unification?

When the Yuan defiled our Chinese land with their rank and膻 odor, Heaven truly grew disgusted with them and therefore gave the Mandate to our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu). Possessing the virtue of a great sage and riding the destiny of a flying dragon, he had ministers like Yi Yin on his left and Zhonghui on his right, the Duke of Zhou before him and Taigong Wang behind. At a single wave of his heavenly halberd, the four quarters responded like an echo. Rising up from Liyang, he flew across the natural moat of the Yangzi River and established his imperial capital at Jinling (Nanjing). Thereupon he annihilated the powerful Han regime of Chen Youliang, struck down the usurping Wu regime of Zhang Shicheng, pacified Jing and Chu, subjugated Min (Fujian) and Guang (Guangdong and Guangxi), and brought order to the regions east and west of the Taihang Mountains and north and south of the Yellow River. Having captured the Yuan capital (Dadu), he then struck into Guanzhong and Shaanxi, swept through Ba and Shu (Sichuan), and gathered in Diannan (Yunnan). The myriad regions came together in allegiance, and the barbarian tribes of the four quarters came to acknowledge his suzerainty.

He united all the territory in the realm and organized it into commanderies and counties; he united all the frontier passes in the realm and fortified them with walls and moats; he united all the farmers in the realm and apportioned their fields and boundary paths; he united all the scholars in the realm and placed them in schools and academies; he united all the merchants and artisans in the realm and arranged them in markets and shops; he united all the barbarians in the realm and clad them in Chinese caps and robes. For rewarding the good there are ranks of nobility, and for punishing the wicked there are penal laws, so that no one in the realm dares to trifle with them; for enriching the state there are taxes, and for defending the people there are troops, so that no one in the realm dares to defy them; for diplomatic audiences and assemblies there are rites, …

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
婚喪有儀章服有等器用有式而天下不
敢越也豈特車同軌而書同文哉又豈特
國不異政而家不殊俗哉
聖子神孫重光継照丙魏在廷孫吳在邊龔黃
卓魯在郡縣至于今百年之間土宇加闢
政教益宣但見室宇華麗人物阜蕃天下
之城邑皆同百貨山積貿易成群天下之
闤闠皆同大袗峩冠談道德而服仁義者
林立天下之學皆同桑穀奮張牛羊茁壯
===
雲布而霧散天下之野皆同舟艫銜車轂
擊人肩摩而踵接天下之道路皆同刁斗
不鳴士馬精強而不試天下之邊皆同東
之夷西之戎南之蠻北之狄山梯海航以
獻方物于
殿陛之下者視
國初尤眾一統之盛若此豈漢唐宋所可伍
哉抑不惟漢唐宋雖三代以前或未之逮
也何則有苗荊蠻今郡縣也犬戎獫狁今

punctuated: 婚喪有儀，章服有等，器用有式，而天下不敢越也。豈特車同軌而書同文哉？又豈特國不異政而家不殊俗哉？聖子神孫，重光継照，丙、魏在廷，孫、吳在邊，龔、黃、卓、魯在郡縣，至于今百年之間，土宇加闢，政教益宣。但見室宇華麗，人物阜蕃，天下之城邑皆同；百貨山積，貿易成群，天下之闤闠皆同；大袗峩冠，談道德而服仁義者林立，天下之學皆同；桑穀奮張，牛羊茁壯，雲布而霧散，天下之野皆同；舟艫銜，車轂擊，人肩摩而踵接，天下之道路皆同；刁斗不鳴，士馬精強而不試，天下之邊皆同；東之夷、西之戎、南之蠻、北之狄，山梯海航以獻方物于殿陛之下者，視國初尤眾。一統之盛若此，豈漢、唐、宋所可伍哉？抑不惟漢、唐、宋，雖三代以前，或未之逮也。何則？有苗、荊蠻，今郡縣也；犬戎、獫狁，今
translation_en:
…marriages and funerals have their rites, insignias and robes have their ranks, and vessels and implements have their standards, so that the empire dares not transgress them. How could this merely be carriages sharing the same gauge and writing sharing the same script? And how could it merely be states having no differing governance and families having no divergent customs?

Sacred sons and divine grandsons have radiated successive brilliance. With Bing Ji and Wei Xiang at court, Sun Wu and Wu Qi on the frontiers, and Gong Sui, Huang Ba, Zhuo Mao, and Lu Gong in the commanderies and counties, down to the present—over the span of a hundred years—the territory has been further opened up, and governance and moral instruction have been ever more widely proclaimed. One sees only magnificent dwellings and an abundant populace: the walled cities and towns of the empire are all alike. The hundred goods are piled like mountains and traders gather in crowds: the marketplaces of the empire are all alike. Wearing grand robes and tall caps, those who discourse on the Way and its Virtue and practice benevolence and righteousness stand thick as a forest: the schools of the empire are all alike. Mulberries and grain flourish and spread, while cattle and sheep grow stout and strong, blanketing the land like clouds and mist: the fields of the empire are all alike. Prows and sterns follow one another, carriage hubs clash, and people rub shoulders and follow on each other's heels: the roads of the empire are all alike. The night-watch bells do not sound, and troops and horses are elite and strong yet go untested: the frontiers of the empire are all alike. The Yi of the east, the Rong of the west, the Man of the south, and the Di of the north, scaling mountains and sailing seas to present local tribute beneath the steps of the throne, are even more numerous than at the founding of the dynasty.

Such flourishing of grand unity—how could the Han, Tang, or Song be ranked alongside it? Indeed, not only the Han, Tang, and Song, even the era of the Three Dynasties and before perhaps did not reach this. Why is that? The Youmiao and the Man of Jing are now commanderies and counties; the Quanrong and Xianyün are now…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
臣妾也若今雲貴之藩瓊儋之郡安南日
本琉球占城之封國以至奴兒干都司之
衛所一百八十四烏思藏都司之衛所三
十三暹羅麻剌蘇祿彭亨等來朝之國三
十七速温河暑地迷河等入貢之地五十
八此皆三代以前杳乎未之聞者用是觀
之古今一統之盛信乎莫盛於我
國家者矣昔我
英宗睿皇帝嘗命儒臣采天下之圖志而萃之
===
名曰
大明一統志
聖藻天葩序其首簡謂昭我一統之盛而且望
天下之士出庸于國以維持一統之盛於
無窮於乎
皇天眷命奄有四海其我
高廟之謂乎
聖謨洋洋嘉言孔彰其我
睿皇之謂乎愚也嘆洛水詠卷阿鋪張

punctuated: 臣妾也。若今雲、貴之藩，瓊、儋之郡，安南、日本、琉球、占城之封國，以至奴兒干都司之衛所一百八十四，烏思藏都司之衛所三十三，暹羅、麻剌、蘇祿、彭亨等來朝之國三十七，速温河、暑地迷河等入貢之地五十八，此皆三代以前杳乎未之聞者。用是觀之，古今一統之盛，信乎莫盛於我國家者矣。昔我英宗睿皇帝嘗命儒臣采天下之圖志而萃之，名曰《大明一統志》，聖藻天葩，序其首簡，謂昭我一統之盛，而且望天下之士出庸于國，以維持一統之盛於無窮。於乎！「皇天眷命，奄有四海」，其我高廟之謂乎！「聖謨洋洋，嘉言孔彰」，其我睿皇之謂乎！愚也嘆洛水，詠卷阿，鋪張
translation_en:
…subjects and servants. As for the present provinces of Yunnan and Guizhou, the prefectures of Qiongzhou and Danzhou, the enfeoffed kingdoms of Annam, Japan, Ryukyu, and Champa, extending even to the one hundred and eighty-four guards and battalions of the Nurgan Regional Military Commission, the thirty-three guards and battalions of the Ü-Tsang Regional Military Commission, the thirty-seven kingdoms coming to court to pay homage such as Siam, Melaka, Sulu, and Pahang, and the fifty-eight tribute-bearing territories such as the Suwen River and the Shudimi River—all of these were utterly unheard of in or before the Three Dynasties. Viewed in this light, throughout antiquity and the present, the flourishing of grand unification has truly never been greater than that of our Dynasty.

Formerly, our Emperor Yingzong Rui ordered the Confucian courtiers to gather the maps and gazetteers of the realm and compile them together, naming the work the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi). With imperial literary brilliance and heavenly blossoms of prose, he wrote a preface for its opening pages, stating that it manifests the flourishing of our grand unification, and furthermore expressing his hope that the scholars of the realm would come forth to be employed by the state in order to sustain this flourishing of grand unification without end.

Alas! "August Heaven favored the mandate, and he possessed all within the Four Seas"—does this not speak of our Exalted Ancestor (Emperor Taizu)? "The sacred counsels are vast and wide, the admirable words are splendidly manifest"—does this not speak of our Emperor Rui (Yingzong)? Unworthy as I am, I sigh in admiration over the Luo River and chant the ode "Juan'e," setting forth at length…

translation_en:
…whose reverence ascends daily like Tang’s and whose benevolence covers all like Heaven as Yao’s did. You reduced the imperial table to avert disasters in Qi and Lu, and summoned recluses to consult on governance in the palace halls; nurturing worthy talents, you bestowed the Nine Classics upon the schools, and preserving the lives of the people, you withdrew the Six Armies from Chanyuan. Specially descending from the Ninefold Palace, you performed the Feng sacrifice at Mount Tai and the Shan sacrifice at Sheshou; once again setting in motion the Ten Thousand Chariots, you graced Qufu with an imperial visit and proceeded to the Confucian Forest. With the phoenix carriage advancing in harmonious majesty [?], you gloriously opened the walls of several fathoms; with the dragon countenance solemn and reverent, you personally beheld the richness of the ancestral temple and the百官 [all the officials/furnishings]. Illustrious indeed is the augmentation of the posthumous title of “Mystic Sage,” honoring him beyond the Tang emperors; grand indeed is the performance of the Tailao sacrifice, according him rites weightier than those of Han Gaozu. Grace extends to his household, and enfeoffments are added to his deceased father and mother; baskets are heavy with gifts of coin and silk, and his distant descendants are generously bathed in the rain and dew of imperial favor. Since antiquity, there has never been anything more magnificent than today!

Your servant Shengyou has only a rough acquaintance with the Odes and the Rites, and has yet to grasp the teaching of broadening through learning and restraining through ritual. Rejoicing to encounter an era of flourishing virtue that exalts moral worth, I am deeply ashamed that I fail to emulate the worthiness of my bygone ancestor. Fortunate to be bathed in vast blessings and appointed to an office to uphold the rites, how dare Your servant not be reverent and respectful morning and night so as to live up to the Court’s gracious mandate? Though my sincerity inclines toward you like the sunflower and bean leaf toward the sun, my repayment lacks even a drop of water or a speck of dust. Still I earnestly hope that the Yellow River will bring forth the Diagram and the Luo River will bring forth…

書，人文載盛；行同倫，車同軌，國統益弘。聖壽天長，皇圖山固。臣不勝感激之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首，謹言。

translation_en:
…[the Yellow River produces the] Chart and the Luo River produces the Writing, so that human culture flourishes greatly; conduct follows the same moral principles and carriages run on the same gauge of tracks, so that the dynasty's unifying rule expands ever wider. May Your Sacred Longevity endure as long as heaven, and the Imperial Domain stand as firm as the mountains! Overwhelmed by the utmost gratitude, Your servant respectfully presents this memorial of thanks for Your Majesty's hearing. In utmost awe and trepidation, bowing his head to the ground, Your servant respectfully speaks.

Question One

Xu Jin 許晋

Taken together with his work in the previous sessions, all of which is superior, elevating him to first place among the many scholars truly accords with public sentiment.

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zheng 鄭: His point-by-point responses are detailed and clear, and his brushwork is vigorous and bold. Compared with all the other compositions, none surpasses his; truly it may be said that when the thoroughbred steed appears, the whole herd of horses is left behind.

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皆化腐成奇蓋老學也
聖製道學品評三策沉詳實參之前場義明而暢論贍而老可以弁多士矣
九丘與八索而並垂禹貢偕二典而不朽
何者立文異而垂訓同也我
國家
列聖重光作典垂訓
太祖高皇帝之大誥三編所以為天下戒也
太宗文皇帝之為善陰隲孝順事實與
宣宗章皇帝之五倫書皆所以為天下勸也至
我
英宗睿皇帝乃命儒臣編輯
大明一統志所以載萬國之幅員而兼百代
之文獻然山川古蹟之內人物名宦之中
所載有惡者焉蓋使人視之以為戒亦
大誥之旨也所載有善者焉蓋使人視之以
為勸亦
為善陰隲孝順事實與五倫書之旨也況夫
折衷嘗出于

punctuated:
皆化腐成奇，蓋老學也。聖製、道學、品評三策，沉詳實，參之前場，義明而暢，論贍而老，可以弁多士矣。

《九丘》與《八索》而並垂，《禹貢》偕《二典》而不朽，何者？立文異而垂訓同也。我國家列聖重光，作典垂訓。太祖高皇帝之《大誥三編》，所以為天下戒也；太宗文皇帝之《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》，與宣宗章皇帝之《五倫書》，皆所以為天下勸也。至我英宗睿皇帝，乃命儒臣編輯《大明一統志》，所以載萬國之幅員，而兼百代之文獻。然山川古蹟之內、人物名宦之中，所載有惡者焉，蓋使人視之以為戒，亦《大誥》之旨也；所載有善者焉，蓋使人視之以為勸，亦《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》與《五倫書》之旨也。況夫折衷嘗出于
translation_en:
…all transform the stale into the marvelous; truly, he is a seasoned scholar. His three policy essays on the Imperial Compositions, the Learning of the Way, and the Evaluation of Historical Figures are profound, detailed, and substantive. Taken together with his essays from the earlier sessions—where his expositions are clear and fluent, and his discourses rich and mature—he is worthy of standing at the head of the multitude of scholars.

The Nine Regions (Jiuqiu) has been handed down alongside the Eight Trigrams (Basuo), and the Tribute of Yu (Yugong) endures immortally together with the Two Canons (Erdian). Why is this? Because although their literary forms differ, the moral instructions they impart are the same. In our Dynasty, a succession of sacred emperors has shone with renewed brilliance, composing canons to hand down instruction. The Three Compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao sanbian) by Emperor Taizu, the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi), was meant to serve as a warning to the empire; the Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and the True Records of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi) by Emperor Taizong, the Cultured Emperor (Wen Huangdi), together with the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) by Emperor Xuanzong, the Accomplished Emperor (Zhang Huangdi), were all meant to serve as encouragement to the empire. Coming to our Emperor Yingzong, the Wise Emperor (Rui Huangdi), he commanded Confucian officials to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi), thereby recording the territory of the myriad realms while encompassing the documents and worthies of a hundred generations. Yet among its mountains, rivers, and ancient sites, and amidst its local figures and eminent officials, there are evil ones recorded therein—this is to cause people to look upon them and take warning, which is also the purport of the Grand Pronouncements; and there are good ones recorded therein—this is to cause people to look upon them and take encouragement, which is also the purport of the Secret Merits of Doing Good, the True Records of Filial Piety, and the Book of the Five Human Relationships. How much more so given that its final judgments once issued from…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖心序首寔形於
天語得非與前四書相為表裏而可同垂於萬
世者乎愚嘗伏而讀之首南北
兩京次江浙閩蜀兩山三廣以及乎河陝
雲貴之十三布政司皆首圖而次志蓋周
官職方氏掌天下之圖而後世若山海圖
若輿地圖者夥矣小史掌邦國之志而後
世若十道志九域志者繁矣合圖與志此
一統志所以善也周之時文武宅鎬京以
===
處上游周公營洛邑以宅土中而宋亦有
東京西京之建舜之時分天下為十二州
而其後有漢之十三部唐之十道宋之十
五路即今兩京十三布政司之制也志之
所載槩而論之若五嶽之高大四瀆之深
廣雲夢望諸之浩博則天下之山川也如
唐之勤儉魏之鄙嗇陳之奢侈鄭衛之淫
靡則天下之風俗也若二程之出河南三
蘇之出眉山韓范之鎮陝右趙張之治京

punctuated: 聖心，序首寔形於天語，得非與前四書相為表裏，而可同垂於萬世者乎？愚嘗伏而讀之，首南北兩京，次江、浙、閩、蜀、兩山、三廣，以及乎河、陝、雲、貴之十三布政司，皆首圖而次志。蓋《周官》職方氏掌天下之圖，而後世若《山海圖》、若《輿地圖》者夥矣；小史掌邦國之志，而後世若《十道志》、《九域志》者繁矣。合圖與志，此《一統志》所以善也。周之時，文、武宅鎬京以處上游，周公營洛邑以宅土中，而宋亦有東京、西京之建。舜之時，分天下為十二州，而其後有漢之十三部、唐之十道、宋之十五路，即今兩京十三布政司之制也。志之所載，槩而論之：若五嶽之高大，四瀆之深廣，雲夢、望諸之浩博，則天下之山川也；如唐之勤儉，魏之鄙嗇，陳之奢侈，鄭、衛之淫靡，則天下之風俗也；若二程之出河南，三蘇之出眉山，韓、范之鎮陝右，趙、張之治京
translation_en:
… the imperial mind, and its opening preface was truly set forth in the Emperor's own words. Does it not complement the four aforementioned books like outside and inside, so that together they may be handed down for ten thousand generations?

I have humbly bowed and read it. Beginning with the Northern and Southern Capitals, and proceeding next to the Thirteen Provincial Administration Commissions—Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Sichuan, Shandong and Shanxi, Huguang, Guangdong, and Guangxi, as well as Henan, Shaanxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou—in every case it places maps first and treatises second. In the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the Director of Regions (Zhifang shi) had charge of the maps of the realm, and in later ages works such as the Maps of Mountains and Seas (Shanhai tu) and the Maps of the Terrestrial Realm (Yudi tu) were numerous; the Lesser Scribe (Xiaoshi) had charge of the records of the states, and in later ages works such as the Treatise on the Ten Circuits (Shidao zhi) and the Treatise on the Nine Regions (Jiuyu zhi) were abundant. Combining maps and treatises—this is why the Comprehensive Gazetteer (Yitong zhi) is so admirable.

In the time of Zhou, Kings Wen and Wu made their dwelling in Haojing so as to occupy the upper reaches, while the Duke of Zhou constructed Luoyi so as to dwell at the center of the land; and the Song likewise had the establishment of the Eastern Capital and Western Capital. In the time of Shun, the realm was divided into twelve provinces, and thereafter came the thirteen regional inspectorates of the Han, the ten circuits of the Tang, and the fifteen routes of the Song—which corresponds to the present system of Two Capitals and Thirteen Provincial Administration Commissions.

To speak in general terms of what is recorded in the treatise: such things as the loftiness and grandeur of the Five Marchmounts, the depth and breadth of the Four Great Rivers, and the vast expanse of the Yunmeng and Mengzhu marshes—these are the mountains and rivers of the realm. Such things as the diligence and frugality of Tang, the meanness and parsimony of Wei, the extravagance of Chen, and the licentiousness and decadence of Zheng and Wei—these are the customs of the realm. Such things as the Two Chengs [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] emerging from Henan, the Three Sus [Su洵, Su Shi 蘇軾, and Su Zhe 蘇轍] emerging from Meishan, Han [Han Qi 韓琦] and Fan [Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹] pacifying Shaanxi, and Zhao [Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢] and Zhang [Zhang Chang 張敞] governing the Capital…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
兆則天下之人物名宦也固不能毛舉而
縷數矣就南畿而舉其尤若應天
帝都其山川則鍾山大江也其風俗則英毅清
邁也紀瞻社稷之臣弘景山中之相何武
刺揚州而政平程顥簿上元而民善非人
物名宦之尤乎鳳陽
帝鄉其山川則荊塗淮淝也風俗則淳厚儉勤
也范滂著清裁於有漢徐達樹大功於
皇明九江宋均之化虎壽春時苗之留犢非人
===
物名宦之尤乎淮揚江淮之雄鎮俗偕剛
勁而淳質也若徐有功之仁胡安定之敎
汲黯卧治於東海張綱弭盜於廣陵又非
人物名宦之尤乎蘇松江湖之奧區俗偕
文雅而奢麗也若范仲淹之相陸遜之將
鄧攸飲水於吳郡丘崈捍海於華亭又非
人物名宦之尤乎至於徐之蕭曹興王之
佐固人物之尤也徽之朱晦菴父子道學
之宗其又尤之尤者耶即是以觀亦足擴

punctuated: 兆，則天下之人物、名宦也，固不能毛舉而縷數矣。就南畿而舉其尤：若應天，帝都，其山川則鍾山、大江也，其風俗則英毅、清邁也；紀瞻社稷之臣，弘景山中之相，何武刺揚州而政平，程顥簿上元而民善，非人物、名宦之尤乎？鳳陽，帝鄉，其山川則荊、塗、淮、淝也，風俗則淳厚、儉勤也；范滂著清裁於有漢，徐達樹大功於皇明，九江宋均之化虎，壽春時苗之留犢，非人物、名宦之尤乎？淮、揚，江、淮之雄鎮，俗偕剛勁而淳質也；若徐有功之仁，胡安定之敎，汲黯卧治於東海，張綱弭盜於廣陵，又非人物、名宦之尤乎？蘇、松，江、湖之奧區，俗偕文雅而奢麗也；若范仲淹之相，陸遜之將，鄧攸飲水於吳郡，丘崈捍海於華亭，又非人物、名宦之尤乎？至於徐之蕭、曹，興王之佐，固人物之尤也；徽之朱晦菴父子，道學之宗，其又尤之尤者耶！即是以觀，亦足擴
translation_en: … the Capital Prefecture (Jingzhao)—these are the notable figures and eminent officials of the empire, whom one certainly cannot enumerate in every detail. Let us take the Southern Metropolitan Area (Nanji) and cite its most outstanding examples. Take Yingtian, the imperial capital: its mountains and rivers are Bell Mountain (Zhongshan) and the Great River (Yangzi), and its customs are heroic, resolute, pure, and lofty. Ji瞻 (Ji Zhan) was a minister of the state altars, and [Tao] Hongjing was the "Prime Minister in the Mountains"; He Wu served as Regional Inspector of Yangzhou and his administration was equitable, while Cheng Hao served as Assistant Magistrate of Shangyuan and the people became good—are these not the most outstanding of notable figures and eminent officials? Take Fengyang, the imperial homeland: its mountains and rivers are Mount Jing, Mount Tu, and the Huai and Fei rivers, and its customs are simple, honest, frugal, and diligent. Fan Pang was renowned for his pure judgment under the Han, and Xu Da established great merit under the August Ming; Song Jun in Jiujiang caused the tigers to reform, and Shi Miao in Shouchun left behind his calf—are these not the most outstanding of notable figures and eminent officials? Take Huai'an and Yangzhou, mighty strongholds between the Yangzi and the Huai: their customs combine vigor and strength with simplicity and substance. Such men as Xu Yougong with his benevolence and Hu Anding (Hu Yuan) with his teaching, or Ji An governing Donghai from his sickbed and Zhang Gang quelling bandits in Guangling—are these again not the most outstanding of notable figures and eminent officials? Take Suzhou and Songjiang, the rich heartland of rivers and lakes: their customs combine literary refinement with luxury and splendor. Such men as Fan Zhongyan as chief minister and Lu Xun as general, or Deng You drinking only water in Wu Commandery and Qiu Chong holding back the sea at Huating—are these again not the most outstanding of notable figures and eminent officials? As for Xiao [He] and Cao [Can] of Xuzhou, aides to a founding king, they were certainly the most outstanding of notable figures; and Zhu Huian (Zhu Xi) and his father of Huizhou, the patriarchs of the Learning of the Way (Daoxue)—are they not the most outstanding of the outstanding! Viewed from these examples alone, it is sufficient to broaden…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
慕遠之懷示為善之規矣况其詳乎然欲
盡書其詳則豈風簷寸晷之可能哉嗟夫
列聖之典同天地之教也語天而不遺一星談
地而不遺一石其疇能之執事取其大而
略其細可也
第二問
道學之傳有自來矣愚甞稽諸渾渾之書
灝灝之書噩噩之書與夫經傳之所載諸
子百家之所傳而知其詳矣盖道之在天
===
下也不可一日而不明亦不可一日而不
行其明也以言其行也以政羲軒同仁而
異化道非不行也然斯時也其民顓蒙其
俗朴畧蚩蚩蠢蠢而羲軒無所用其政至
於堯舜以下則不同矣是故於變於堯風
動於舜永賴於禹允殖於湯咸和於文永
清於武而制作大備於周公其經營措置
莫非惟精惟一之緒餘其運量酬酢莫非
建中建極之推本此道見於治而行也帝

俗朴畧蚩蚩蠢蠢而羲軒無所用其政至
於堯舜以下則不同矣是故於變於堯風
動於舜永賴於禹允殖於湯咸和於文永
清於武而制作大備於周公其經營措置
莫非惟精惟一之緒餘其運量酬酢莫非
建中建極之推本此道見於治而行也帝
punctuated:
慕遠之懷，示為善之規矣，况其詳乎？然欲盡書其詳，則豈風簷寸晷之可能哉？嗟夫！列聖之典，同天地之教也。語天而不遺一星，談地而不遺一石，其疇能之？執事取其大而略其細可也。

第二問
道學之傳有自來矣。愚甞稽諸渾渾之書、灝灝之書、噩噩之書，與夫經傳之所載、諸子百家之所傳，而知其詳矣。盖道之在天下也，不可一日而不明，亦不可一日而不行。其明也以言，其行也以政。羲、軒同仁而異化，道非不行也；然斯時也，其民顓蒙，其俗朴畧，蚩蚩蠢蠢，而羲、軒無所用其政。至於堯、舜以下則不同矣。是故於變於堯，風動於舜，永賴於禹，允殖於湯，咸和於文，永清於武，而制作大備於周公。其經營措置，莫非惟精惟一之緒餘；其運量酬酢，莫非建中建極之推本。此道見於治而行也。帝
translation_en:
…the sentiment of admiring the past and set forth models for doing good—how much more so if we consider their full details! Yet if one wished to write down all those details in full, how could that possibly be done within the brief span of time under the windswept eaves of the examination hall? Alas! The canons of the successive sacred emperors are like the teachings of Heaven and Earth. To speak of Heaven without omitting a single star, or to discuss Earth without leaving out a single stone—who could do that? It will suffice for Your Excellency to take what is great in this and pass over the fine details.

Question Two
The transmission of the Learning of the Way (Daoxue) has a long history. I have examined the "boundless" documents [of Yao and Shun], the "vast" documents [of Xia], and the "solemn" documents [of Shang and Zhou], together with what is recorded in the Classics and commentaries and what has been handed down by the Various Masters and Hundred Schools, and thus I know its details. Now, as the Way exists in the world, it cannot go a single day without being illuminated, nor can it go a single day without being practiced. Its illumination is through words; its practice is through governance. Fuxi and Xuanyuan [the Yellow Emperor] shared the same benevolence yet differed in their transformative influence; it was not that the Way was not practiced. At that time, however, the people were ignorant and untutored, their customs simple and crude, and they were naive and unformed, so Fuxi and Xuanyuan had no occasion to employ their governance. When it came to Yao, Shun, and those after them, things were different. Therefore, the people were transformed under Yao, moved as by the wind under Shun, eternally reliant under Yu, truly flourishing under Tang, brought to universal harmony under King Wen, and forever pacified under King Wu, while institutions and rites were brought to great completion by the Duke of Zhou. Their planning and arrangements were nothing other than the outgrowth of "being refined and being single-minded"; their deliberations and responses to affairs were nothing other than extensions rooted in "establishing the Mean and establishing the Supreme Standard." This was the Way made manifest in governance and put into practice. The emperors…

translation_en: … Emperors and Kings taught through moral virtue and brought their achievements to completion; it was not that the Way was unilluminated. Yet at that time, the common people lived in supreme harmony and the myriad things all accorded with their natures—vast, grand, level, and tranquil—so that Emperors and Kings had no need to utter words. When it came to the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, things were different again. Therefore, the import of the "one thread binding all" was set forth by Confucius (Kongzi 孔子), and the doctrines of the goodness of human nature and the nourishing of vital energy (qi 氣) were set forth by Mencius (Mengzi 孟子). The Way of "beingrefined and single-minded" was merely entrusted to empty words, and the principle of "establishing the mean and establishing the ultimate standard" was not manifested in actual deeds. This was the Way taking form in words and thereby becoming illuminated. The saying about "an eternal long night" was seen at a postal pavilion; although no one knows who wrote it, he was truly someone of genuine insight. Now, when Confucius was alive in his day, even a Second Sage like Yan Hui 顏回 still lifted the hem of his robes and hastened to the corner of the hall to receive the teachings of broadening with learning and restraining with ritual without ever contravening them. How much more so for Mencius, a great worthy who ranked one degree below Yan Hui—had he lived at that time, how could he have driven his doctrines abreast with Confucius's across the empire? When the autumn sun was eclipsed and Mount Tai crumbled, the various scholars from the Han dynasty onward expounded the Classics: for instance, the Book of Documents (Shu 書) of Master Fu (Fu Sheng 伏生), through its transmission to Chao Cuo 鼂錯, fell into corruption and error; the Book of Changes (Yi 易) of Tian He 田何 and the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) of Master Shen (Shen Gong 申公), through the transposition of their arrangement, fell into disorder; the Rites (Li 禮) of Master Gaotang (Gaotang Sheng 高堂生) fell into eclecticism; the exegetical glosses of Wang Su 王肅 and Zheng Xuan 鄭玄 differed from one another; and the Correct Meaning (Zhengyi 正義) of Kong Yingda 孔穎達 was adulterated with prognosticatory apocrypha—how are any of these worth mentioning! Master Dong (Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒) was a pure Confucian scholar, yet he lapsed into the theory of releasing yin and shutting off yang; Yang Xiong 楊雄 was a great Confucian scholar, yet he was benighted by his theory that human nature is a mixture of good and evil; Wang Tong 王通 was also a Master of the Yellow and Fen River region, yet he drowned in…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
續經之罪惟韓子之在唐也迴瀾於東揭
斗於北原道一篇幾似矣然其謂博愛之
謂仁行而宜之之謂義則又舉其用而遺
其體是以振鄒魯之遺風而接孔孟之墜
緒者卒有待於濂洛關閩之數君子焉今
即其所言以究其所行莫不先致力於窮
理次存心於持敬而後體驗於躬行之間
擴充於事為之際其與舜典之精一丹書
之敬義論語之博約孟子之知言養氣一
===
律也而道統先後相繼矣元儒若許衡學
宗朱子窮理以致其知反躬以踐其實吳
澄自致聖賢之道其教人刻意究精微之
蘊反身踐進脩之實然則可以繼朱子者
非二子其誰歟嗚呼文將喪天道未墜地
或者非人為耶抑愚因執事之發策而有
感焉聖賢達而在上則為君為臣而其道
見於治如堯舜如禹湯文武周公者是也
聖賢窮而在下則為師為友而其道著於

punctuated: 續經之罪。惟韓子之在唐也，迴瀾於東，揭斗於北，《原道》一篇幾似矣。然其謂「博愛之謂仁，行而宜之之謂義」，則又舉其用而遺其體。是以振鄒魯之遺風，而接孔孟之墜緒者，卒有待於濂、洛、關、閩之數君子焉。今即其所言以究其所行，莫不先致力於窮理，次存心於持敬，而後體驗於躬行之間，擴充於事為之際，其與《舜典》之精一、《丹書》之敬義、《論語》之博約、《孟子》之知言養氣一律也，而道統先後相繼矣。元儒若許衡，學宗朱子，窮理以致其知，反躬以踐其實；吳澄自致聖賢之道，其教人刻意究精微之蘊，反身踐進脩之實。然則可以繼朱子者，非二子其誰歟？嗚呼！文將喪天，道未墜地，或者非人為耶？抑愚因執事之發策而有感焉。聖賢達而在上，則為君為臣，而其道見於治，如堯、舜，如禹、湯、文、武、周公者是也；聖賢窮而在下，則為師為友，而其道著於
translation_en: … the offense of presuming to continue the Classics. Only Master Han [Han Yu 韓愈] in the Tang dynasty turned back the raging waves toward the east and held aloft the Dipper in the north; his essay "Tracing the Way" (Yuandao 原道) came close indeed. Yet when he stated that "universal love is called humaneness, and acting so as to be appropriate to it is called righteousness," he spoke of their function while omitting their substance. Therefore, reviving the remaining ethos of Zou and Lu and reconnecting the fallen thread of Confucius and Mencius ultimately had to await the several gentlemen of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng 程 brothers, Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹]. Now, if we examine their deeds in light of their words, every one of them first devoted his efforts to fathoming principle, next preserved his mind through maintaining reverence, and thereafter realized it personally in his own conduct and extended it in the course of his affairs. This is completely of one rule with the "refinement and singleness" of the Canon of Shun (Shundian 舜典), the "reverence and righteousness" of the Cinnabar Writing (Danshu 丹書), the "broad learning and restraint" of the Analects (Lunyu 論語), and the "understanding of words and nourishing of vital氣 (qi)" of the Mencius (Mengzi 孟子)—and thus the succession of the Way (daotong 道統) was carried on from one to the next. Among the Confucian scholars of the Yuan dynasty, such as Xu Heng 許衡, his learning took Master Zhu [Zhu Xi] as its ancestor, fathoming principle to extend his knowledge and reflecting upon himself to put its reality into practice; while Wu Cheng 吳澄 personally attained the Way of the sages and worthies, and in teaching others he applied his mind earnestly to investigating the subtle and profound stores and reflecting upon himself to practice the reality of advancing in self-cultivation. If this is so, then who if not these two masters could succeed Master Zhu? Alas! When culture is about to be lost, Heaven does not let the Way fall to the ground—is this perhaps not the doing of men alone? Moreover, in my ignorance I have been moved to reflection by the policy question posed by Your Excellency. When sages and worthies attain high station above, they act as rulers and ministers, and their Way is manifested in governance—such were Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou. 學寥寥經生舉子則辭章記誦以為工此
口耳之學明之者昧之也賢士大夫則權
謀術數以為尚此功利之學行之者塞之

書，如孔、孟，如周、程、朱者是也。叔世以来，聖學寥寥。經生舉子，則辭章記誦以為工，此口耳之學，明之者昧之也；賢士大夫，則權謀術數以為尚，此功利之學，行之者塞之也，又烏知有所謂聖賢大學之道哉？惟我聖明紹洪圖之宥密，撫文運之亨嘉。六經既纂，其道明矣，猶御經筵以求斯道之形於言者；四海既治，其道行矣，猶廣言路以求斯道之推於治者。玉堂鴻儒、鸞坡宿學，必有道以輔之，然莫要乎聖賢大學之道。愚也亦竊有志，執事倘不鄙而與其進也，則當挟是以往。

第三問
賀元忠
同考試官教授韓 批：條答詳明，可以措諸行事，有用之材也。
同考試官監丞閻 批：當豐之時而能言保豐之道，必識時務者歟！
translation_en:
… writings, such as Confucius and Mencius, and such as Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi. Since the ages of decline, the learning of the sages has grown sparse and solitary. Students of the Classics and examination candidates take ornate composition and rote memorization as their craft—this is learning of the mouth and ear, where those who would clarify the Way actually obscure it. Worthy scholar-officials esteem权谋 (expedient schemes) and statecraft techniques—this is learning of utility and profit, where those who would practice the Way actually obstruct it. How then could they know that there is such a thing as the Way of the Great Learning of the sages and worthies?

Only our sacred and enlightened sovereign has succeeded to the profound and tranquil great enterprise and presides over a prosperous and auspicious era of literary culture. The Six Classics having been compiled, their Way is already clear; yet His Majesty still attends the Classics Colloquium (jingyan) to seek how this Way takes form in words. The Four Seas having been brought to order, their Way is already practiced; yet His Majesty still broadens the avenues of speech to seek how this Way may be extended in governance. The great Confucian scholars of the Jade Hall and the veteran scholars of the Luan Slope [the Hanlin Academy] must certainly have the Way with which to assist Him, yet nothing is more essential than the Way of the Great Learning of the sages and worthies. I, though humble, also venture to cherish this aspiration. Should Your Excellency not disdain me and instead grant me advancement, then I shall hold fast to this and go forward.

Third Question
He Yuanzhong 賀元忠

Associate Examiner, Proctor (jiancheng) Yan, comments: In a time of abundance, to be able to speak of the Way of preserving abundance—surely he is one who understands the affairs of the times!

text:
考試官侍講徐批此篇所論時務鑿鑿可行
必有學識者
考試官洗馬楊批所答皆可見諸行事豈徒
言哉
惟時惟幾舜以儆其臣無怠無荒益以戒
其君夫有虞之時雍熈泰和之治也其君
臣尚相儆戒若此然則有天下國家者當
豐亨豫大之時可無維持經久之慮乎謹
因明問而陳之夫百口之家歷數世之久
===
則養必有所不贍事必有所不濟况今天
下之大當百年之治則夫民物雖豐而或
病於水旱兵馬雖豐而或乏於營陣文武
之選雖豐而或庶官多闕緩急無裨者亦
其勢然也為政者任其勢而不思所以善
之則其後必有不勝其患者可無慮乎夫
民之所以病於水旱者以農穀稀而儲積
寡也今宜驅游惰以服田禁奢侈以歸儉
重官吏侵漁之刑謹義倉預備之政如古

言哉
惟時惟幾舜以儆其臣無怠無荒益以戒
其君夫有虞之時雍熙泰和之治也其君
臣尚相儆戒若此然則有天下國家者當
豐亨豫大之時可無維持經久之慮乎謹
因明問而陳之大百口之家歷數世之久
===
則養必有所不贍事必有所不齊況今天
下之大當百年之治則夫民物雖豐而或
病於水旱兵馬雖豐而或乏於營障文武
之選雖豐而或歷員多關緩急無稗者亦
其勢然也爲政者任其勢而不思所以善
之則其後必有不勝其患者可無慮乎夫
民之所以病於水旱者以農穀稀而儲積
寡也今宜驅游惰以服田禁奢侈以歸儉
重官吏侵漁之刑謹義倉預備之政如古
punctuated:
考試官侍講徐批：此篇所論時務，鑿鑿可行，必有學識者。
考試官洗馬楊批：所答皆可見諸行事，豈徒言哉！

「惟時惟幾」，舜以儆其臣；「無怠無荒」，益以戒其君。夫有虞之時，雍熈泰和之治也，其君臣尚相儆戒若此。然則有天下國家者，當豐亨豫大之時，可無維持經久之慮乎？謹因明問而陳之。夫百口之家，歷數世之久，則養必有所不贍，事必有所不濟。况今天下之大，當百年之治，則夫民物雖豐而或病於水旱，兵馬雖豐而或乏於營陣，文武之選雖豐而或庶官多闕、緩急無裨者，亦其勢然也。為政者任其勢而不思所以善之，則其後必有不勝其患者，可無慮乎？夫民之所以病於水旱者，以農穀稀而儲積寡也。今宜驅游惰以服田，禁奢侈以歸儉，重官吏侵漁之刑，謹義倉預備之政，如古
translation_en:
Examiner and Expositor-in-waiting Xu comments: The current affairs discussed in this essay are concrete and practicable; he must be a man of learning and insight.
Examiner and Librarian of the Heir Apparent Yang comments: Everything in his reply can be put into actual practice; how could these be mere empty words!

"Be attentive to the time and to the subtle signs"—thus Shun admonished his ministers; "do not be indolent, do not be negligent"—thus Yi cautioned his sovereign. Now, the age of Yu [Shun] was an era of harmonious, flourishing, and supreme peace, yet its ruler and ministers still admonished and cautioned one another like this. If so, then when those who possess the Empire and the state find themselves in a time of abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness, how can they lack plans for sustaining and preserving it over the long term? I respectfully set forth my views in response to your perceptive question. Now, when a household of a hundred mouths endures through several generations, its sustenance will inevitably fall short in some respects, and its affairs will inevitably fail to succeed in others. How much more so with the vastness of the Empire today, after a hundred years of peaceful rule! Thus, that the people and material goods, though abundant, sometimes suffer from floods and droughts; that soldiers and horses, though abundant, are sometimes lacking in the camps and battle formations; and that candidates selected for civil and military office, though abundant, sometimes leave many official posts vacant and prove of no help in emergencies—all this is likewise the natural tendency of circumstances. If those who govern merely drift along with this tendency without pondering how to remedy it, then afterward there will inevitably be calamities too great to bear. Can one afford not to take thought? Now, the reason the people suffer from floods and droughts is that agricultural grain is scarce and stored reserves are meager. Today we ought to drive the idle and lazy back to working the fields, prohibit extravagance so as to return to frugality, stiffen the punishments for officials and clerks who peculate and prey upon the people, and attend carefully to the administration of charitable granaries and preparedness, just as in antiquity…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
者三年耕有一年之食九年耕有三年之
食則歉歲其有困乎兵之所以乏其精者
以較閱不嚴而尺籍多虛名也今宜申私
役之令革月錢之弊老弱者盡汰之慵惰
者嚴練之如古者戎車三百咸若熊羆虎
賁三千盡如虓虎兵其有不精乎馬所以
乏其壯者以濫收曠養而閑廐多虛數也
今宜監牧必擇其善攻駒必收其良借乘
者有罰盜殺者無宥如古者驌皇騂騏莫
===
非臧材驒駱駰騢無不徂作則馬其有不
壯者乎至若文武之臣則官以雜襲功以
冒進而武不皆才也資格有限門徑無窮
而文不皆賢也今宜黜倖人飭世胄練之
成其材鼓之作其氣功不容妄奏罪不至
輕原如古者君必知將將必知兵則武臣
其有不才乎革冗濫却奔競有闕隨注而
勿稽有賢輙用而毋緩考課嚴明舉選公
正如古者建官惟賢涖事惟能則文臣其

translation_en:
…in antiquity, when three years of plowing left one year's surplus of food, and nine years of plowing left three years' surplus of food, would there be any distress in lean years?

The reason troops lack elite vigor is that inspections and reviews are not strict, and the military registers are filled with empty names. Today we ought to reiterate the prohibitions against using soldiers for private labor, abolish the abuse of monthly payments in lieu of service, thoroughly weed out the old and weak, and strictly drill the indolent and lazy. If, as in antiquity, the three hundred war chariots were all like bears and grisly bears, and the three thousand brave guards were all like roaring tigers, how could the troops fail to be elite?

The reason horses lack sturdy vigor is that they are indiscriminately accepted and neglectfully reared, and the corrals and stables are full of empty numbers. Today we ought to ensure that pasture supervisors are chosen for their competence, that in breaking colts only the fine ones are kept, that those who borrow horses for private riding are punished, and that those who steal or slaughter them are shown no leniency. If, as in antiquity, the bay-and-white, yellow-and-white, red, and piebald steeds were all of fine quality, and the dappled, white-maned, gray, and roan horses all stepped forth with vigor, then how could the horses fail to be sturdy?

As for civil and military officials: because offices are inherited indiscriminately and merits are claimed fraudulently for advancement, military officers are not all talented; because seniority qualifications are rigid while backdoor channels are endless, civil officials are not all worthy. Today we ought to dismiss those who advance by unearned favor, discipline the hereditary lineages, train them to bring their talents to maturity, and rouse them to stir up their spirit; merits must not be falsely reported, and offenses must not be lightly pardoned. If, as in antiquity, the ruler invariably knows his generals and the generals invariably know their troops, then how could military officials fail to be talented? We should eliminate superfluous and abusive appointments, reject unscrupulous office-seeking, fill vacancies promptly without delay, and employ the worthy at once without hesitation, making performance evaluations strict and clear and selections fair and impartial. If, as in antiquity, offices are established only for the worthy and affairs are administered only by the capable, then how could civil officials…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
有不賢者哉此五者天下之事之大者也
而執事復疑有大焉是非愚生所敢知也
其他若鹽利入於勢家宜出之以惠商也
工匠役於私門宜檢之以歸公也馬船橫
於河路宜禁之以恤民也刑罰弛於姑息
宜飭之以禁奸也百事替於因循宜作之
以除弊也若此者安能悉數之哉今
聖天子如舜恒懷惟時惟幾之儆賢大臣如益
屢進無怠無荒之戒制治保邦將世之億
===
萬世而無疆矣尚俟愚言之贅哉
第四問
上同

尤雄壯明白較之前二場其書經中之巨擘歟

translation_en:
… fail to be worthy? These five matters are the great affairs of the realm. Yet Your Excellency further doubts whether there are even greater ones; that is not something this foolish student dares to know. As for other matters: where salt profits flow into powerful families, they ought to be released in order to benefit the merchants; where artisans are conscripted into private households, they ought to be inspected and returned to public service; where horse-transport boats act lawlessly along the river routes, they ought to be prohibited in order to show compassion for the people; where punishments have grown lax through indulgence, they ought to be tightened in order to suppress the wicked; where all manner of affairs have fallen into decline through routine negligence, they ought to be roused into action in order to eradicate abuses. How could matters such as these all be enumerated? Today, the Sacred Son of Heaven is like Shun, constantly cherishing the admonition to be timely and attentive to the subtle; the worthy grand ministers are like Yi, repeatedly presenting the warning against indolence and dissipation. Securing order before disorder arises and preserving the state, this rule shall be handed down for hundreds of millions of generations without end—what need is there to wait upon the superfluous words of this foolish one!

Fourth Question
Same [author] as above.

Associate Examiner Professor Fang comments: All five policy essays are resplendent with literary brilliance, and the piece on the Three Powers (Heaven, Earth, and Man) is especially vigorous and clear. Compared with the first two sessions, he must be a leading figure among the candidates specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing)!
Examiner Expositor-in-waiting Xu comments: The policy essay is well-grounded in historical evidence.
Examiner Librarian Yang comments: It discusses the Way in which the sages handle the Three Powers thoroughly…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
無遺策乎也
人君以一身出而為天地人之宗主惟欲
盡其裁成輔相之道以立人極之則也三
才之責既盡則聖人之能事畢矣粵稽邃
古黃帝始作盖天以定氣敬乎天矣然其
制未詳也至唐虞命羲和以造璣衡仰觀
以齊七政作曆以授人時斯術不違天而
政不失時矣嗣是漢落下閎乃經營之鮮
于妄人又量度之耿壽昌始鑄銅為象宋
===
錢樂又鑄銅作渾天儀厥後宋又因之為
儀三重其在外曰六合儀次其內曰三辰
儀其最在內曰四遊儀其法雖有所增損
至此為益精矣是其觀天之象雖益精而
欽若昊天窺璣齊政何在也果能如唐虞
理天道者乎黃帝始畫野分州經土設井
因乎地矣其法未備也至帝堯命神禹以
平水土弼成五服以建諸侯咸則三壤以
制井田斯官有分封之土民有衣食之仰

無遺策乎也

盡其裁成輔相之道以立人極之則也三
才之責既盡則聖人之能事畢矣粤稽遂
古黄帝始作蓋天以定氣數乎天矣然其
制未詳也至唐虞命羲和以造璣衡仰觀
以齊七政作曆以授人時斯其術亦違天而
政不失時矣嗣是漢落下閎乃經營之鮮
于妄人又量度之耿壽昌始鑄銅爲象宋
===
錢樂又鑄銅作渾天儀厥後宋又因之爲
儀三重其在外曰六合儀次其内曰三辰
儀其最在内曰四遊儀其法雖有所增損
至此爲益精矣是其觀天之務雖益精而
欽若昊天璣衡齊政何在也果能如唐虞
理天道者乎黄帝始畫野分州經土設井
因乎地矣其法未備也至帝堯命神禹以
平水土獮成五服以建諸侯咸則三壤以
制井田斯官有分封之土民有衣食之仰
punctuated:
無遺策乎？也。
人君以一身出而為天地人之宗主，惟欲盡其裁成輔相之道，以立人極之則也。三才之責既盡，則聖人之能事畢矣。粵稽邃古，黃帝始作盖天以定氣，敬乎天矣，然其制未詳也。至唐虞命羲和以造璣衡，仰觀以齊七政，作曆以授人時，斯術不違天而政不失時矣。嗣是，漢落下閎乃經營之，鮮于妄人又量度之，耿壽昌始鑄銅為象，宋錢樂又鑄銅作渾天儀。厥後，宋又因之為儀三重：其在外曰六合儀，次其內曰三辰儀，其最在內曰四遊儀。其法雖有所增損，至此為益精矣。是其觀天之象雖益精，而欽若昊天、窺璣齊政何在也？果能如唐虞理天道者乎？黃帝始畫野分州，經土設井，因乎地矣，其法未備也。至帝堯命神禹以平水土，弼成五服以建諸侯，咸則三壤以制井田，斯官有分封之土，民有衣食之仰…
translation_en:
…without leaving anything out; a true policy essay [?]!

The ruler emerges in his own person to serve as the sovereign master of Heaven, Earth, and Man, desiring only to fulfill the Way of regulating and assisting them so as to establish the standard of the ultimate of human perfection. Once his responsibilities toward the Three Powers are fulfilled, the sage’s work is complete. Examining remote antiquity, the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) first created the gaitian (canopy-heaven) model to determine the seasonal pneuma, thereby showing reverence toward Heaven; yet its system was not yet detailed. Coming to the eras of Tang and Yu (Yao 堯 and Shun 舜), Xi 羲 and He 和 were commanded to construct the jade-cogged armillary sphere and sighting tube (jiheng 璣衡), looking up to observe and thereby bring into order the Seven Regulators (sun, moon, and five planets), and creating a calendar to grant the seasons to the people. Thus their art did not contravene Heaven and governance did not miss the proper seasons. Thereafter, in the Han dynasty, Luoxia Hong 落下閎 planned and constructed it, Xianyu Wangren 鮮于妄人 measured and calibrated it, and Geng Shouchang 耿壽昌 first cast bronze to make a celestial globe; in the Liu-Song dynasty, Qian Le 錢樂 [Qian Yuezhi 錢樂之] again cast bronze to make an armillary sphere (huntianyi 渾天儀). Subsequently, the Song dynasty built upon these to make an instrument of three concentric rings: the outermost was called the Instrument of the Six Directions (liuheyi 六合儀), the next inside it was called the Instrument of the Three Luminaries (sanchenyi 三辰儀), and the innermost was called the Instrument of the Four Roaming Components (siyouyi 四遊儀). Although the methods underwent additions and reductions, by this point they had become ever more precise. Yet even though their instruments for observing the celestial phenomena grew ever more precise, where were the reverent accord with vast Heaven and the peering through the sighting tube to bring order to governance? Could they truly match the way Tang and Yu ordered the Way of Heaven? The Yellow Emperor first delineated the wilds and divided the provinces, surveying the land and establishing the well-field system, thereby adapting to Earth; yet his methods were not yet complete. Coming to Emperor Yao, he commanded the divine Yu 禹 to pacify the waters and the land, to assist in completing the Five Zones (wufu 五服) in order to establish the feudal lords, and to grade all soils into three classes in order to institute the well-fields. Thus officials had enfeoffed lands and the people had the means on which to rely for food and clothing…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣継是周公之營洛國有郊甸縣有都鄙
大司徒又以土宜之法辯十有二土以任
土事至漢又分天下為十三部唐分為十
道宋分為十五路其疆理皆不合乎古亦
各因其形勢而已是其土宇之域不加小
而祇台德先敬天之休何有也又能如帝
王理地道者乎人處乎兩間古聖人制禮
樂之教兵刑之政以治之聖者之世尚乎
教故唐虞伯夷典禮后夔典樂而兵刑臯
===
陶兼之王者之世崇乎政故成周司寇掌
刑司馬掌政而禮樂宗伯兼之此帝王之
所以不同也夫子之從先進以禮樂文質
之適中彼玉帶孝孫之禮樂有是乎惟宋
朱子家禮愛敬本質之是崇蔡元定律呂
新書本原器數之咸備乃得其遺意矣先
王之用兵刑無非仁義之所在彼八衛九
章之兵刑有是乎惟宋太祖慮法網太密
鞭笞殿陛之不施漢太祖制兵有其道寛
alt_text:
矣繼是周公之營洛國有都鄙縣有都鄙
大司徒又以土宜之法辯十有二土以任
土事至漢又分天下為十三部唐分為十
道宋分為十五路其疆理皆不合乎古亦
各因其形勢而已是其土宇之域不加小
而祗台德先敬天之休何有也又能如帝
王理地道者乎人處乎兩間古聖人制禮
樂之教兵刑之政以治之聖者之世尚乎
教故唐虞伯夷典禮后夔典樂而兵刑皐
===
陶兼之王者之世崇乎政故成周司寇掌
刑司馬掌政而禮樂宗伯兼之此帝王之
所以不同也夫子之從先進以禮樂文質
之適中彼玉帶孝孫之禮樂有是乎惟宋
朱子家禮愛敬本質之是崇蔡元定律呂
新書本原器數之咸備乃得其遺意矣先
王之用兵刑無非仁義之所在彼八衛九
章之兵刑有是乎惟宋太祖憲法綱太密
鞭笞嚴陛之不施漢太祖制兵有其道寬
punctuated:
矣。継是周公之營洛，國有郊甸，縣有都鄙，大司徒又以土宜之法辯十有二土，以任土事。至漢又分天下為十三部，唐分為十道，宋分為十五路，其疆理皆不合乎古，亦各因其形勢而已。是其土宇之域不加小，而「祇台德先」、「敬天之休」何有也？又能如帝王理地道者乎？

人處乎兩間，古聖人制禮樂之教、兵刑之政以治之。聖者之世尚乎教，故唐、虞伯夷典禮，后夔典樂，而兵刑臯陶兼之；王者之世崇乎政，故成周司寇掌刑，司馬掌政，而禮樂宗伯兼之。此帝王之所以不同也。夫子之從先進，以禮樂文質之適中，彼玉帶、孝孫之禮樂有是乎？惟宋朱子《家禮》，愛敬本質之是崇；蔡元定《律呂新書》，本原器數之咸備，乃得其遺意矣。先王之用兵刑，無非仁義之所在，彼八衛、九章之兵刑有是乎？惟宋太祖慮法網太密，鞭笞殿陛之不施；漢太祖制兵有其道，寛…
translation_en:
… Following this, when the Duke of Zhou built Luoyang, the state had its suburbs and royal domain, and the districts had their towns and outlying villages; the Minister of Education (Dasitu) also used the method of soil suitability to distinguish the twelve types of soil in order to assign agricultural tasks. By the Han dynasty, the realm was further divided into thirteen Regions; in the Tang, it was divided into ten Circuits; and in the Song, into fifteen Circuits. None of their territorial administrations conformed to antiquity; each merely adapted to its own topographical conditions. Thus, while the expanse of their territories did not grow any smaller, what did they have of "reverently leading with virtue" or "respecting the blessings of Heaven"? And how could they govern the Way of Earth like the Emperors and Kings of antiquity?

Humanity dwells between Heaven and Earth, and the ancient sages instituted the teachings of ritual and music and the governance of military affairs and punishments in order to rule them. The era of the sages esteemed teaching; thus under Tang Yao and Yu Shun, Boyi 伯夷 directed rituals, Hou Kui 后夔 directed music, while Gao Yao 臯陶 concurrently handled military affairs and punishments. The era of the true kings revered governance; thus in the Zhou dynasty, the Minister of Justice (Sikou) was in charge of punishments, the Minister of War (Sima) was in charge of military administration, while the Minister of Rites (Zongbo) concurrently handled rituals and music. This is why the Five Emperors and the Three Kings differed. Confucius followed the men of former times because in ritual and music they achieved the proper balance of refinement and substance; did the rituals and music of Li Yudai 李玉帶 and Zu Xiaosun 祖孝孫 possess this? Only in the Song dynasty did Master Zhu's (Zhu Xi 朱熹) Family Rituals (Jiali) revere the fundamental substance of love and reverence, and Cai Yuanding's 蔡元定 New Treatise on Pitch-Pipes (Lülü xinshu) fully encompass both fundamental principles and instruments and numbers, thereby capturing their bequeathed meaning. The former kings' use of military force and punishments was nothing less than the embodiment of benevolence and righteousness; did the military and penal systems of the Eight Guards and the Nine Chapters possess this? Only Emperor Taizu of Song, concerned that the net of the law was too dense, refrained from administering whipping and flogging in the palace courtyard; and Emperor Taizu of Han (Liu Bang 劉邦) had the proper way of controlling the military, combining leniency…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
猛嚴密之兼致亦有可取矣是其政敎非
虞周之政敎又能如虞周之理人道乎噫
三代以上之君因三才之道而理之有其
制而有實三代以下之君循先王之迹而
理之有其制而無實無其實亦虛器耳我
聖明在上因唐虞三代之制體唐虞三代之實
嚴恭寅畏對越
上帝于
宸極包涵徧覆運量四海于
===
淵衷萬邦之民又皆欲囿於政敎之中然
萬幾之繁不能獨理故立欽天監以典曆象
建司空以掌邦土禮樂典於宗伯太常兵
刑掌於司寇司馬由是人時授而歲功以
成四民居而地利以興神人治而上下以
和暴亂刑而邦國以平其裁成輔相之道
直與唐虞三代匹休而漢唐宋風斯下矣
愚生斯世何幸躬逢其盛
第五問

虞周之政教又能如虞周之理人道乎噫
三代以上之君因三才之道而理之有其
制而有實三代以下之君循先王之迹而
理之有其制而無實無其實亦虛器耳我
聖明在上因唐虞三代之制體唐虞三代之實
嚴恭寅畏對越
上帝于
宸極包涵徧覆運量四海于
===
淵衷萬邦之民又皆欲囿於政教之中然
萬幾之繁不能獨理故立欽天監以典曆象
建司空以掌邦土禮樂典於宗伯太常兵
刑掌於司寇司馬由是人時授而歲功以
成四民居而地利以興神人治而上下以
和暴亂刑而邦國以平其裁成輔相之道
直與唐虞三代匹休而漢唐宋風斯下矣
愚生斯世何幸躬逢其盛
第五問
punctuated:
猛嚴密之兼致，亦有可取矣。是其政敎非虞、周之政敎，又能如虞、周之理人道乎？噫！三代以上之君，因三才之道而理之，有其制而有實；三代以下之君，循先王之迹而理之，有其制而無實。無其實，亦虛器耳。我聖明在上，因唐、虞、三代之制，體唐、虞、三代之實，嚴恭寅畏，對越上帝于宸極；包涵徧覆，運量四海于淵衷，萬邦之民又皆欲囿於政敎之中。然萬幾之繁，不能獨理，故立欽天監以典曆象，建司空以掌邦土，禮樂典於宗伯、太常，兵刑掌於司寇、司馬。由是人時授而歲功以成，四民居而地利以興，神人治而上下以和，暴亂刑而邦國以平。其裁成輔相之道，直與唐、虞、三代匹休，而漢、唐、宋風斯下矣。愚生斯世，何幸躬逢其盛！
第五問
translation_en:
… combining leniency and severity with rigor and precision, also had merits worth adopting. Yet since their governance and moral instruction were not those of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou, how could they match Yu and the Zhou in ordering the way of humanity?

Alas! The rulers of the Three Dynasties and earlier ordered the world by following the way of the Three Powers [Heaven, Earth, and Man]; they possessed both the institutional forms and the reality. The rulers after the Three Dynasties ordered the world by merely following the traces of the former kings; they possessed the institutional forms without the reality. Without the reality, institutions are nothing more than empty vessels!

Our Sacred and Enlightened Sovereign sits on high, adopting the institutions of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties, and embodying their reality. With solemn reverence and respectful awe, He responds to the Supreme Lord on High from the Imperial Throne; all-embracing and universally sheltering, He encompasses and measures the Four Seas within His profound mind, wishing that the people of all states may be embraced within His governance and instruction. Yet the myriad affairs of state are too numerous to be managed alone. Therefore, He has established the Directorate of Astronomy (Qintian jian) to take charge of the calendar and astronomical phenomena, and instituted the Minister of Works (Sikong) to manage the territory of the realm; rites and music are administered by the Minister of Rites (Zongbo) and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (Taichang), while military affairs and punishments are managed by the Minister of Justice (Sikou) and the Minister of War (Sima). Consequently, the seasons are granted to the people and the year's agricultural labors are brought to completion; the four classes of people are settled and the benefits of the earth are desarrollada and raised up; spirits and humans are well governed and superiors and inferiors are in harmony; the violent and rebellious are punished and the states of the realm are at peace. His way of regulating and assisting nature truly rivals the splendor of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, leaving the ethos of the Han, Tang, and Song far behind. Born into this age, how fortunate am I to witness such flourishing glory in person!

Question Five

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
濮晉
觀古人之行治而議其是非評其優劣皆
反諸身而戒之勉之此亦格物之學進德
之功也執事舉以敎之敢不敬承乎請得
陳之伯夷聖之清柳下惠聖之和皆百世
之師也文彥博侍朝以臣道而恭程頤侍
講以師道而莊各得其當矣樂伯之左射
以菆攝叔之右入壘各行所聞於致師耳
無足論也若夫子路受牛而勸德子貢讓
===
金而止善皆聖門之高弟也而止善不如
勸德齊桓公正而不譎晉文公譎而不正
皆五伯之雄也而譎不如正姚崇之通宋
璟之介皆為名相也而璟優於崇文翁之
柔常爽之剛皆善立敎也而爽劣於翁李
廣郭子儀之寬程不識李光弼之嚴皆為
漢唐之良將然不識子儀非二李可擬其
賢也趙廣漢以術破奸黨韓延壽以禮和
寇讐皆為潁川之名守也然用術何如用

punctuated:
濮晉

觀古人之行治，而議其是非，評其優劣，皆反諸身而戒之勉之，此亦格物之學，進德之功也。執事舉以敎之，敢不敬承乎？請得陳之。伯夷聖之清，柳下惠聖之和，皆百世之師也。文彥博侍朝以臣道而恭，程頤侍講以師道而莊，各得其當矣。樂伯之左射以菆，攝叔之右入壘，各行所聞於致師耳，無足論也。若夫子路受牛而勸德，子貢讓金而止善，皆聖門之高弟也，而止善不如勸德；齊桓公正而不譎，晉文公譎而不正，皆五伯之雄也，而譎不如正；姚崇之通，宋璟之介，皆為名相也，而璟優於崇；文翁之柔，常爽之剛，皆善立敎也，而爽劣於翁；李廣、郭子儀之寬，程不識、李光弼之嚴，皆為漢唐之良將，然不識、子儀非二李可擬其賢也；趙廣漢以術破奸黨，韓延壽以禮和寇讐，皆為潁川之名守也，然用術何如用
translation_en:
Pu Jin 濮晉

To observe the conduct and governance of the ancients, to discuss their right and wrong, and to evaluate their superiority and inferiority—turning all of this back upon oneself as a warning and an encouragement—this too is the learning of investigating things and the work of advancing in virtue. Since Your Excellency has raised this to instruct us, how dare I not respectfully receive it? Allow me to set it forth.

Boyi 伯夷 was the sage of purity, and Liuxia Hui 柳下惠 was the sage of harmony; both are teachers for a hundred generations. Wen Yanbo 文彥博 attended court with reverence according to the way of a minister, while Cheng Yi 程頤 attended the imperial lectures with solemnity according to the way of a teacher; each attained what was proper. As for Le Bo 樂伯 on the left shooting with fine arrows, and She Shu 攝叔 on the right entering the enemy ramparts, each merely practiced what he had heard regarding challenging the enemy to battle, which is not worth discussing.

As for Zilu 子路 accepting a cow and thereby encouraging virtue, and Zigong 子貢 declining gold and thereby putting a stop to good deeds: both were eminent disciples of the Sage's school, yet stopping good deeds is not as good as encouraging virtue. Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓公 was upright and not crafty, while Duke Wen of Jin 晉文公 was crafty and not upright: both were heroes among the Five Hegemons, yet craftiness is not as good as uprightness. Yao Chong's 姚崇 adaptability and Song Jing's 宋璟 integrity made both famous Grand Councilors, yet Jing was superior to Chong. Wen Weng's 文翁 gentleness and Chang Shuang's 常爽 firmness were both effective in establishing instruction, yet Shuang was inferior to Weng. The leniency of Li Guang 李廣 and Guo Ziyi 郭子儀, and the strictness of Cheng Bushi 程不識 and Li Guangbi 李光弼, made them all fine generals of the Han and Tang dynasties; yet in their worthiness, Bushi and Ziyi cannot be matched by the two Lis. Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 usedstratagems to break up wicked factions, while Han Yanshou 韓延壽 used ritual propriety to reconcile bitter enemies: both were famous Grand Protectors of Yingchuan 潁川, yet how can using stratagems compare to using…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
禮巫馬期任已而勞宓子賤任人而逸皆
為單父之賢令也然任己豈如任人魯男
子拒隣之嫠婦而不納雖未若柳下惠之
嫗不逮門之女而不亂然亦善學柳下惠
者也管寧與華歆同鋤地見金也寧視與
瓦石無異歆取而擲之寧豈不優於歆乎
是皆優劣之可見者至於帝堯之聖如天
而桀則地也八凱之善如薰而四凶則蕕
也子文之治兵非子玉之剛而無禮者可
===
比鞭箠不必計也仕宦者當如陳遵之苦
身自約而毋放意自恣如張竦焉奏事者
當如韓休之力爭而毋順旨如蕭嵩焉司
刑者當如于定國徐有功之恕而毋刻如
張湯來俊臣焉奉使者當如梁琛之專美
本朝而毋微說國弊如郝晷焉軍門夜閉
者當如段志玄之不納君使而毋納之如
宇文士及焉則是非皆可見矣至若禮貴
得中則子張除喪鼓琴而和子夏除喪鼓

translation_en: …propriety? Wuma Qi 巫馬期 relied on himself and toiled, whereas Fu Zijian 宓子賤 relied on others and was at ease; both were worthy magistrates of Shanfu 單父, yet how could relying on oneself compare to relying on others? The man of Lu 魯 refused his neighbor, a widow, and would not let her in; although he did not match Liuxia Hui 柳下惠, who sheltered a woman who could not reach her gate in time with his body without impropriety, he was nonetheless one who learned well from Liuxia Hui. When Guan Ning 管寧 and Hua Xin 華歆 were hoeing the ground together and saw gold, Ning regarded it as no different from tiles and stones, whereas Xin picked it up and then threw it away; was Ning not superior to Xin? In all these cases, superiority and inferiority can be seen. As for the sageliness of Emperor Yao 帝堯, it was like heaven, whereas Jie 桀 was like the earth; the goodness of the Eight Harmonious Ones (Bakai 八凱) was like fragrant herbs, whereas the Four Criminals (Sixiong 四凶) were like foul weeds. Ziwen's 子文 training of troops cannot be compared with that of Ziyu 子玉, who was rigid and lacked propriety; the use of whips and rods need not even be reckoned. Those who serve in office ought to be like Chen Zun 陳遵 [? textual inversion of Zhang Song and Chen Zun], who disciplined himself through hardship, and not indulge themselves willfully like Zhang Song 張竦; those who submit memorials on state affairs ought to be like Han Xiu 韓休, who strove forcefully in remonstrance, and not comply with imperial wishes like Xiao Song 蕭嵩; those in charge of punishments ought to have the leniency of Yu Dingguo 于定國 and Xu Yougong 徐有功, and not be harsh like Zhang Tang 張湯 and Lai Junchen 來俊臣; those who serve as envoys ought to be like Liang Chen 梁琛, who exclusively praised his own court, and not subtly speak of his state's flaws like Hao Gui 郝晷; those who close the military camp gates at night ought to be like Duan Zhixuan 段志玄, who refused to admit the sovereign's envoy, and not admit him like Yuwen Shiji 宇文士及. Thus right and wrong can all be seen. As for propriety valuing the attainment of the mean: when Zizhang 子張 completed his mourning and strummed the zither, the sound was already harmonious, whereas when Zixia 子夏 completed his mourning and strummed…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
琴而不和過不及均失中也管仲鏤簋朱
紘而難為上晏嬰豚肩不掩豆而難為下
濫與隘均失中也天命有德則顏峻之嗔
而與人官謝莊之笑而不與人官者皆非
矣天討有罪則暴勝之多所誅殺王賀之
多所縱舍者皆非矣夫即前數十人之是
非優劣而論別之亦格物之事也其是者
士所當勉而其非者士所當戒取其是而
優者尤加勉焉亦進德之功也學伊川晞
===
廣平以上企乎八凱之勳聖堯之德豈非
愚之志哉雖然定輕重者衡也別妍媸者
鑑也愚何足以別古人之是非而定其優
劣也哉執事人物之衡鑑也幸進而教之
alt_text:
琴而不和過不及均失中也管仲鏤簋朱
紘而難為上晏嬰豚肩不掩豆而難為下
濫與隘均失中也天命有德則顏峻之嘖
而與人官謝莊之笑而不與人官者皆非
矣天討有罪則慕勝之多所誅殺王賀之
多所縱舍者皆非矣夫即前數十人之是
非優劣而論别之亦格物之事也其是者
士所當勉而其非者士所當戒取其是而
優者尤加勉焉亦進德之功也學伊川晞
廣平以上企乎八凱之勲耶堯之德豈非
愚之志哉雖然定輕重者衡也别妍蚩者
鑑也愚何足以别古人之是非而定其優
劣也哉執事人物之衡鑑也幸進而教之
punctuated: 琴而不和，過、不及均失中也；管仲鏤簋朱紘而難為上，晏嬰豚肩不掩豆而難為下，濫與隘均失中也。天命有德，則顏峻之嗔而與人官、謝莊之笑而不與人官者，皆非矣；天討有罪，則暴勝之多所誅殺、王賀之多所縱舍者，皆非矣。夫即前數十人之是非優劣而論別之，亦格物之事也。其是者，士所當勉；而其非者，士所當戒。取其是而優者尤加勉焉，亦進德之功也。學伊川，晞廣平，以上企乎八凱之勳、聖堯之德，豈非愚之志哉？雖然，定輕重者，衡也；別妍媸者，鑑也。愚何足以別古人之是非而定其優劣也哉？執事，人物之衡鑑也，幸進而教之。
translation_en:
… played the zither and its notes were not yet in harmony—going too far and falling short equally miss the mean. Guan Zhong 管仲 used carved grain vessels and red cap-strings, making it hard for those above him; Yan Ying 晏嬰 offered a suckling pig's shoulder that did not even cover the platter, making it hard for those below him—extravagance and parsimony equally miss the mean. Since Heaven charges the virtuous, both Yan Jun 顏峻, who granted offices to people while scowling in anger, and Xie Zhuang 謝莊, who withheld offices from people while smiling, were in the wrong. Since Heaven punishes the guilty, both Bao Shengzhi 暴勝之, who executed and killed many, and Wang He 王賀, who pardoned and let go many, were in the wrong.

Now, to examine these several dozen men mentioned above and distinguish their right and wrong, their superiority and inferiority, is also a matter of the investigation of things (gewu 格物). What was right in them is what a scholar ought to strive for, and what was wrong in them is what a scholar ought to guard against. To adopt what is both right and superior among them and strive after it all the more is likewise the work of advancing in virtue. To study Yichuan 伊川 (Cheng Yi 程頤) and emulate Guangping 廣平 (Song Jing 宋璟), so as to aspire upward to the achievements of the Eight Harmonious Ones (Bakai 八凱) and the virtue of the sage Yao 堯—is this not indeed my humble aspiration? Even so, what determines weight is the balance, and what distinguishes beauty from ugliness is the mirror. How could someone as foolish as I suffice to distinguish the right and wrong of the ancients and determine their superiority and inferiority? Your Excellencies are the balance and mirror of human character; I earnestly hope that you will bring me forward and instruct me.

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
上天眷命人君必篤生賢才
以遺之天能遺之而不能成
之而成之則在於君必躬行
以表正之學校以作養之及
其道明則又設科目簡用之
以圖治化斯天意之所在而
===
亦君道之所當盡也故重華
正德以闢四門建極敷言以
宅三俊虞周於斯為盛矣我
祖宗奉
天撫運立極敷文以開億萬年之
鴻業何莫不由於斯欽惟
皇上以至聖大德重光

應天府鄉試錄後序

上天眷命人君，必篤生賢才以遺之。天能遺之而不能成之，而成之則在於君。必躬行以表正之，學校以作養之；及其道明，則又設科目簡用之，以圖治化。斯天意之所在，而亦君道之所當盡也。故重華正德以闢四門，建極敷言以宅三俊，虞、周於斯為盛矣。我祖宗奉天撫運，立極敷文，以開億萬年之鴻業，何莫不由於斯？欽惟皇上以至聖大德，重光
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

When High Heaven looks with favor upon a ruler and grants him its Mandate, It invariably brings forth men of worth and talent to bequeath to him. Yet while Heaven can bequeath them, It cannot bring them to completion; bringing them to completion rests with the ruler. He must set an upright example through his own personal conduct and nurture them through schools; and once the Way is illuminated among them, he must establish examination categories to select and employ them, thereby pursuing transformative governance. Herein lies the will of Heaven, and it is likewise what the Way of the ruler ought to fulfill to the utmost. Thus Chonghua [Shun] rectified his virtue and threw open the four gates, and the kings of Zhou established the supreme standard and difunded their teachings so as to place men of the three grades of eminence in office; the eras of Yu [Shun] and Zhou reached their flourishing height in this. Our Imperial Ancestors received Heaven's Mandate and guided the destiny of the realm, establishing the supreme standard and spreading civil culture to inaugurate the grand enterprise of a myriad ages—how could any of this not have derived from this same principle? We reverently reflect that His Majesty the Emperor, with utmost sageliness and great virtue, has renewed the brilliance of…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
烈祖嗣統以來兩科于兹矣成化
辛卯之秋復當大比應天府
府尹臣亨府丞臣哲先期奏
請考試官例應文學侍從之
臣
上命臣守陳臣瓊往涖其事臣等欽
承
===
制命夙夜祇懼入院考較惟慎
惟公時合太學畿內之士暨
庶人在官者奇二千三百取
其文足以顯道者百三十有
五人遵故典也臣竊惟
朝廷今日所用亮天功熙庶績
之賢才亦惟

punctuated: 烈祖，嗣統以來，兩科于兹矣。成化辛卯之秋，復當大比。應天府府尹臣亨、府丞臣哲，先期奏請考試官，例應文學侍從之臣。上命臣守陳、臣瓊往涖其事。臣等欽承制命，夙夜祇懼。入院考較，惟慎惟公。時合太學、畿內之士暨庶人在官者奇二千三百，取其文足以顯道者百三十有五人，遵故典也。臣竊惟朝廷今日所用亮天功、熙庶績之賢才，亦惟
translation_en: … the Illustrious Progenitors. Since succeeding to the imperial line, two examination cycles have taken place up to the present. In the autumn of the xinmao year of the Chenghua era (1471), it was once again the time for the triennial examination. The Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, your servant Heng, and the Vice Prefect, your servant Zhe, submitted a memorial in advance requesting Examiners, who by precedent should be literary and attendant officials. His Majesty commanded your servant Shouchen and your servant Qiong to go and oversee the affair. Your servants reverently received the imperial mandate, filled with awe and trepidation day and night. Upon entering the examination compound to evaluate and compare the papers, we strove only for caution and impartiality. At the time, combining the scholars from the Imperial University and the capital region together with commoners serving in official posts, there were over two thousand three hundred candidates. From among them, we selected one hundred and thirty-five men whose essays were sufficient to manifest the Way, in accordance with established precedent. Your servant venture to reflect that the worthy talents employed by the Court today to assist in Heaven's work and make all achievements resplendent are likewise solely…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上天純佑
皇上以啓
文明之盛治而畀
列聖成之於前日也今日所成之
賢才極藹藹濟濟之盛於是
簡其尤者而升用之又將資
其相與保
===
鴻休荅
天眷於無疆此臣等所以不敢不
慎簡以副
聖意也凡與賓興之士可不知所
自重乎繼自今當激昂奮發
增益其所未至期策名禮闈
進而對揚

punctuated: 上天純佑皇上，以啓文明之盛治，而畀列聖成之於前日也。今日所成之賢才，極藹藹濟濟之盛，於是簡其尤者而升用之，又將資其相與保鴻休、荅天眷於無疆。此臣等所以不敢不慎簡，以副聖意也。凡與賓興之士，可不知所自重乎？繼自今，當激昂奮發，增益其所未至，期策名禮闈，進而對揚
translation_en:
…that High Heaven has purely blessed His Majesty so as to initiate a flourishing rule of cultural brilliance, and entrusted the succession of Sacred Emperors to cultivate them in days gone by. The worthy talents cultivated today have reached the utmost abundance of a thriving and dignified multitude. Thereupon, selecting the most outstanding among them and promoting them for employment, the court will further rely on them to work together in preserving the great blessings and answering Heaven's favor without end. This is why your servants dared not fail to be cautious in our selection so as to fulfill the Sacred Intention.

How could all you scholars who have participated in this ceremonial recommendation of guests fail to know how to conduct yourselves with self-respect? From this day forward, you ought to rouse yourselves to vigorous effort and augment what you have not yet attained, aspiring to have your names inscribed on the roster of the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites, and advancing to respond to and extol…

title: 成化七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
清問蔚然起而為名進士其服
列為臣尤當弘惇厚溥博之
德量操光明正大之心術以
為之本為直而不為佞為良
而不為憸以德輔世而不阿
世以公奉法而不蠹法致
君為堯舜禹湯文武之聖化民底
===
唐虞三代之隆戒敕維持用
洽雍熙於悠久奠
宗社於不拔斯不負
聖天子成之以道而資之所以保
所以荅也而前日賢才輔成
之偉績豈得專美乎諸士子
尚勵翼焉豈惟不負於

列爲臣尤當弘惇厚溥博之
德量操光明正大之心術以

而不爲憸以德輔世而不阿
世以公奉法而不蠹法致

宗社於不拔斯不負
聖天子成之以道而資之所以保
所以咨也而前日賢才輔成
之偉績豈得專美乎諸士子
尚勵翼焉豈惟不負於
punctuated: 清問，蔚然起而為名進士。其服列為臣，尤當弘惇厚溥博之德量，操光明正大之心術，以為之本。為直而不為佞，為良而不為憸，以德輔世而不阿世，以公奉法而不蠹法，致君為堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之聖，化民底唐、虞、三代之隆，戒敕維持，用洽雍熙於悠久，奠宗社於不拔。斯不負聖天子成之以道，而資之所以保、所以荅也。而前日賢才輔成之偉績，豈得專美乎？諸士子尚勵翼焉，豈惟不負於
translation_en: … the Emperor's august inquiries, rising resplendently to become renowned metropolitan graduates (jinshi). When they enter office and take their places in the ranks of officials, they must especially broaden a moral capacity that is generous, sincere, vast, and far-reaching, and maintain a disposition of mind that is upright, honorable, and impartial as their foundation. They should be straightforward and not sycophantic, virtuous and not deceitful; they should assist the world through virtue rather than pander to the world, and uphold the law with public-spiritedness rather than corrupt the law. They should help the Sovereign become a sage like Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, and transform the people so as to attain the flourishing prosperity of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, exercising vigilance and maintenance so as to diffuse harmonious peace for a long time to come and establish the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain on an unshakable foundation. In this way they will not fail the Sacred Son of Heaven, who perfected them through the Way and relies upon them to preserve his great blessings and answer the favor of Heaven. How then could the magnificent achievements of the worthy talents who assisted in governance in former days monopolize all the glory? May all you scholars strive and exert yourselves in support! Not only will you not fail …
